newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Bid values Bank Melbourne at 2.1 times net assets.
newsitem.headline: Bid values Bank Melbourne at 2.1 times net assets.

text.p: Bank of Melbourne Ltd said on Thursday the agreed A$1.435 billion offer from Westpac Banking Corp valued Bank of Melbourne at 2.1 times net assets and represented a multiple of 15.2 times prospective 1997 earnings.
The Bank said this was comparable to the 2.1 times net assets paid by St George for Advance Bank and the 2.1 time net assets paid by Westpac to Challenge shareholders.

"The Bank of Melbourne has enjoyed strong growth since its inception in 1989 with our total assets increasing from A$3.0 nillion to A$11.3 billion and net profit after tax increasing by 325 percent from A$19.7 million to A$84 million," said the Bank's chairman Christopher Stewart said.
He added that the premium over net assets of A$695 million which Westpac has offered recognises the strategic value of the strong retail franchise that the bank has built.
"It also takes account of the benefits of the operational efficiencies to be achieved by combining the two organistaions," Stewart said.

He said that on completion of the merger schemes Bank of Melbourne would continue with its own chief executive officer, who, with a senior executive team comprised of Bank of Melbourne and Westpac executives, would be responsible for the day-to-day combined retail operations of both the Bank of Melbourne and Westpac in Victoria.
